next_step: DE-0010-R1 (code/tests/docs only, on top of the disabled safe baseline 63bb46d7957fbbd514f0b571564cb4a66da9d65b) has closed three exact-head trust gaps found after DE-0010 merged and was then disabled pending review, across two remediation cycles. Cycle 1: (1) supervisor-verdicts.mjs's standalone ACCEPTED marker previously included the Markdown blockquote marker '>' in its harmless-decoration character class alongside bold/italic/heading markers, so a blockquoted/reply-quoted `> ACCEPTED — exact head <sha>` line could be misread as a genuine acceptance; '>' is no longer part of that decoration class. (2) supervisor-ci.mjs matched governance CI evidence by the fixed workflow name and file path alone, which proves which file path produced a run but not which content GitHub actually loaded from it - a same-repository pull request could rewrite .github/workflows/project-governance.yml itself and still land a completed, successful, name+path-matching run at its own exact head; evaluateGovernanceEvidence/isGovernanceWorkflowFileTrusted additionally require the exact governance workflow file bytes at the pull request's head to match the repository's default-branch copy before a run is ever reported as 'success'. Cycle 2 (this remediation, after an independent exact-head Codex review found cycle 1 incomplete): byte-identity of the workflow file alone still let a same-repository pull request leave that file untouched while tampering with package.json's own npm script definitions, tsconfig.json/vitest.config.ts, the governance validator (scripts/validate-project-governance.mjs), or any of its transitive helpers under scripts/ or test/, and still land a genuinely successful, byte-trusted run. evaluateGovernanceEvidence now additionally requires that changedFilePaths - every file GitHub's compare API reports as different between the pull request's own recorded base branch and its exact head, fetched independently of PR content by the new fetchChangedFilePaths wiring - contains no file matching the new isGovernanceDecisionPathFile (the workflow file, package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, or any file under scripts/ or test/, matched by directory prefix so a newly added file cannot evade it). Any mismatch on either trust check, or an unreadable/missing comparison on either side, is reported as the 'untrusted' conclusion, which supervisor-policy.mjs treats exactly like a CI failure (dispatches ci_failed, never merge_ready) regardless of any owner ACCEPTED verdict recorded at that same head. All three fixes are covered by regression tests, including a same-name/path 'success' run that tampers with package.json and/or the governance validator while the workflow file itself stays byte-identical, and clean exact-head success for ordinary application-code changes under src/. The documented trust boundary: because this check cannot distinguish a legitimate scripts/test change from a malicious one, any pull request touching scripts/ or test/ - including this remediation's own new regression tests - is itself reported 'untrusted' and requires a human owner's exact-head review and explicit ACCEPTED verdict rather than automated merge-ready dispatch. Cycle 3 (this remediation, after a second independent exact-head Codex review found cycle 2 incomplete): two further deterministic bypasses closed. First, GitHub's compare API caps a single comparison at 300 changed files, but changedFilePaths was trusted as complete evidence even at or above that cap, so a pull request touching more than 300 files could place a decision-path edit past the cap where it would never appear in the returned list; evaluateGovernanceEvidence now also reports 'untrusted' whenever changedFilePaths.length reaches CHANGED_FILE_EVIDENCE_COMPLETENESS_CAP (300), regardless of what the (necessarily incomplete) list does or does not contain. Second, the fixed decision-path file set protected only the exact filenames package.json/tsconfig.json/vitest.config.ts, but npm install also resolves dependencies through package-lock.json/npm-shrinkwrap.json/yarn.lock when present, and Vitest/Vite recognize several further config/workspace filename variants (vitest.config/vitest.workspace/vitest.projects/vite.config, each across six extensions) capable of changing which tests run or how; GOVERNANCE_DECISION_PATH_FILES now also lists the lock/shrinkwrap inputs and the new GOVERNANCE_DECISION_PATH_CONFIG_PATTERN matches every supported extension of those four config/workspace basenames, so a previously-unlisted variant this repository does not currently use (e.g. vitest.workspace.ts) can no longer evade the check. Both fixes are covered by regression tests, including a changed-file list at exactly the 300-file cap (untrusted) versus one file below it with only ordinary src/ changes (trusted success), and an added package-lock.json or vitest.workspace.ts alongside a byte-identical workflow file (untrusted). Separately, the two workflow-file structural test suites (autonomy-wake-workflow.test.mjs, autonomy-supervisor-workflow.test.mjs) remain skipped via describe.skipIf while both DE-0010 workflow YAML files stay intentionally absent from every code-only branch pending review; neither workflow file was restored, modified, merged, or live-tested by this work packet.
